name: Alan Aragon
who: MS in Nutrition Science; founder of the Alan Aragon Research Review, one of the longest-running peer-vetted nutrition/fitness research digests, plus a history of consulting physique and combat athletes.
why: Set the template for research-literate fitness nutrition writing that dozens of later newsletters copied; still active and cited after decades.
reach: IG and X combined roughly 300K (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Danny Lennon
who: MSc in Nutrition & Sports Performance; founder of Sigma Nutrition, a long-running evidence-based podcast and CPD education company for nutrition professionals.
why: One of the most consistently rigorous interview-format nutrition podcasts, widely used by dietitians and coaches for continuing education.
reach: Niche podcast audience, low tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Idrees Mughal (Dr. Idz)
who: MBBS plus an MRes in nutrition research; UK-trained physician who debunks carnivore, vegan-extremist, and fad-diet claims at scale on YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram.
why: Among the highest-reach myth-busting voices in the space, using a genuine research background to fact-check viral diet claims in near-real time.
reach: TikTok/IG combined likely well over 1M (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Nicola Guess
who: Registered Dietitian and PhD, University of Oxford; researches low-carbohydrate diets and type 2 diabetes remission, with direct clinical work on diabetes nutrition.
why: Respected voice bridging clinical dietetics and diabetes research, known for pushing back on both low-carb hype and knee-jerk dismissals of it.
reach: Modest academic/public following, low tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Adrian Chavez
who: PhD in Nutritional Sciences; runs a private nutrition coaching practice and hosts a long-running evidence-based nutrition podcast.
why: Steady, credentialed voice translating primary research for both clients and a lay audience without the hype common in the space.
reach: Modest, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Gabrielle Fundaro
who: PhD in Human Nutrition, Foods, and Exercise; coaches clients on gut health and behavior change through an evidence-based physique coaching group.
why: Rare combination of gut-health research depth and applied behavior-change coaching, filling a gap most fitness-nutrition educators skip.
reach: Moderate niche following, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Martin MacDonald
who: SENr-registered nutritionist running Mac-Nutrition Uni and a clinical practice that has worked with British elite athletics and rugby programs.
why: One of the few names on this list whose day job is fueling actual elite teams, not just talking about it online.
reach: Moderate UK following, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Kevin Klatt
who: PhD in Nutritional Sciences (Cornell), postdoctoral researcher at UC Berkeley, and Director of Research at Examine.com.
why: Deep technical rigor on micronutrient and supplement science, shaping how thousands of practitioners interpret primary literature via Examine.
reach: Niche academic/practitioner following on X, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Eric Trexler
who: PhD in Human Movement Science; Director of Research at MASS (Monthly Applied Science in Sport), a peer-reviewed-literature digest for coaches and dietitians.
why: MASS is treated as a reference standard by strength/physique coaches for staying current on primary research without wading through journals themselves.
reach: Combined social roughly 150-250K (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Bill Campbell
who: PhD; directs the Performance & Physique Enhancement Laboratory at the University of South Florida, running real studies on contest-prep and body recomposition with physique athletes.
why: Bridges academic research and practice directly — his lab's contest-prep studies are widely cited across bodybuilding and physique-sport nutrition.
reach: Combined social roughly 200-300K (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Spencer Nadolsky
who: DO, board-certified in obesity medicine and lipidology; treats patients directly on weight and metabolic health and co-hosts the Docs Who Lift podcast.
why: A working physician-nutrition voice in the increasingly loud GLP-1/obesity-medicine conversation, grounded in an active clinical practice.
reach: Combined social roughly 150K+ (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Stuart Phillips
who: PhD, Professor of Kinesiology at McMaster University; the field's leading voice on dietary protein and muscle protein synthesis, especially in older adults.
why: His body of work has directly shaped protein-intake guidance worldwide — a field-leading researcher whose findings changed practice, not just opinion.
reach: Academic/public reach on X, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Rhiannon Lambert
who: Registered Nutritionist (RNutr); founder of the Rhitrition clinic on Harley Street, working with a broad private-client base including athletes.
why: Built one of the UK's best-known private nutrition clinics on credentialed, non-gimmick practice, with a media presence to match.

name: Dr. Federica Amati
who: PhD in nutrition; Chief Nutritionist at ZOE and lecturer at Imperial College London.
why: Public-facing science lead for one of the largest population nutrition-science projects currently running, translating findings for a mass audience.
reach: Personal following tens of thousands, amplified by ZOE's much larger platform (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Dr. Sarah Berry
who: PhD, Professor of Nutritional Sciences at King's College London; lead scientist on ZOE's PREDICT studies, one of the largest personalized-nutrition research programs.
why: PREDICT's scale (100,000+ participants) gives her population-level impact rare among nutrition researchers, and she communicates it directly to the public.
reach: Personal following moderate, amplified by ZOE's platform (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Renee McGregor
who: Registered Dietitian specializing in RED-S (Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport); works clinically with elite endurance athletes and eating-disorder recovery cases.
why: Her RED-S advocacy has changed how sport federations and coaches think about underfueling in athletes, not just how individual clients eat.
reach: Modest-moderate, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

name: Abbey Sharp
who: Registered Dietitian running a private practice, best known for YouTube videos dissecting "what I eat in a day" content and debunking diet-culture claims.
why: Highest reach of any dietitian-credentialed myth-buster on this list, using a large young audience to counter influencer nutrition misinformation directly.

name: Dr. Duane Mellor
who: Registered Dietitian and PhD, senior lecturer at Aston University; regular British Dietetic Association spokesperson on fad diets and nutrition myths in UK media.
why: The go-to credentialed rebuttal voice in British press and broadcast whenever a new diet trend or misinformation claim goes viral.
